prompt:
This project has a Makefile, a tab separated data file data/products.tsv (columns sku, name, category, price_cents, stock, note) and small Python tools in tools/ (read their docstrings; do not change them). Make these changes.

Data file, data/products.tsv, rewritten in place:
- Rename the column price_cents to price and write its values in dollars with exactly two decimals: 1999 becomes 19.99, 5 becomes 0.05, 100000 becomes 1000.00. A row whose price_cents is empty keeps an empty price.
- Add a last column named status: out when stock is 0, low when stock is from 1 to 9, ok when stock is 10 or more.
- Every other field stays exactly as it is, including empty fields (a row whose note is empty still has its tab, so the row has 7 fields with two tabs in a row before the status) and names with quote or non ASCII characters. The file keeps LF line endings and exactly one newline at the end.

Makefile:
1. Change the stats target so it reports on the price column instead of price_cents.
2. Change the COLUMNS variable to 7 so make check expects the new column count.
3. Change the clean target so it removes $(DIST) as well as $(OUT).
4. Add the target $(OUT)/lowstock.tsv with prerequisites $(DATA) and $(OUT). Its recipe runs tools/tsvfilter.py to write the header and the rows whose status is low or out to that file.
5. Add the target $(OUT)/categories.txt with prerequisites $(DATA) and $(OUT). Its recipe writes the sorted, unique category names, one per line, to that file, using tools/tsvcolumn.py and sort -u.
6. Add the phony target dist with prerequisites stats, $(OUT)/lowstock.tsv and $(OUT)/categories.txt. Its recipe creates $(DIST) with mkdir -p and then runs tools/bundle.py to write $(DIST)/bundle.txt from $(OUT)/stats.txt, $(OUT)/lowstock.tsv and $(OUT)/categories.txt, in that order. Add dist to .PHONY.

Use the existing variables (PYTHON, DATA, OUT, DIST) in the new targets instead of writing paths in full, so make OUT=other DIST=other2 dist works. Every recipe line must start with a tab character, and the other lines of the Makefile must stay as they are. The Makefile is checked with a small stand in for make, so keep to the simple style it already uses (variables, $(NAME), $@, $<, $^, explicit rules, .PHONY) and do not use pattern rules, make functions, include or conditionals. Recipes are run with sh.
